title: Russian missile strikes knock out power and water across Ukraine and cause outages in Moldova
body:
On Wednesday, 23 November 2022, Russia launched a new wave of missile strikes that knocked out power and water in several Ukrainian cities, including Kyiv, Lviv and Mykolaiv. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said that 21 of 31 missiles aimed at Kyiv were shot down, a claim that could not be independently verified, and that running water was cut citywide after an infrastructure facility was struck.

National police reported that at least six civilians were killed and more than 30 were injured. Most of Khmelnytskyi region lost power and water, according to regional administrator Serhii Hamalii. Ukrenergo disconnected the Rivne, South Ukraine and Khmelnytskyi nuclear power plants from the grid as a precaution. The reactors were restarted but stayed off the grid, and the Mykolaiv region's nuclear plant was also cut off.

Moldova, which is connected to Ukraine's grid, lost power across more than half of the country, according to its leaders. President Maia Sandu said Russia was purposely killing people and leaving others in the dark and cold. President Volodymyr Zelensky said 4,000 points of invincibility would provide heat, water and phone charging during extended outages. The attacks were part of a campaign against Ukraine's energy system that had been under way since 10 October 2022.
